I am an old woman of 85 years here in Mwanza, and my strength is not what it used to be. This small plot of mine, less than half a hectare, I work together with my grandchildren who help me when they are not at school. I cannot afford the chemical fertilizers from the shop, but I put the manure from my few chickens and goats on the soil, and I save my own seeds from last season like my mother taught me. We depend on the rains here, and I intercrop so that if one crop fails, another may give us food.
